chat.help.title: Chat help
chat.help.askDesc: The standard mode. Claude asks permission before EVERY action that touches your system (editing files, running commands): a card appears and you approve or deny each one.
chat.help.editsDesc: Claude can edit and create files without asking; everything else (terminal commands, network, etc.) still asks for permission. Handy once you trust the direction of the work.
chat.help.allDesc: Advanced acceptance: Claude runs ABSOLUTELY everything without asking — commands, edits, network. It's the riskiest mode (that's why it confirms when you turn it on); use it only when you fully trust the task and want zero friction.
chat.help.planDesc: Claude touches nothing: it just reads the project and drafts a work plan. Ideal to explore an idea or see what it would do before letting it loose.
chat.help.modesFoot: You can change mode at any time; it applies from the next action. The selector color marks the risk: green = controlled · amber = medium · red = accepts everything.
chat.help.iconsIntro: Each Claude action appears in the thread as a two-icon chip: the console (it ran a tool) + the type. Tap the chip to see the full detail; the border marks the result (green ok · red error).
chat.help.pacIntro: The same Pac-Man appears up here and in the Sessions cards — the color AND the movement tell you what the conversation is doing at each moment:
chat.help.pacWorkingDesc: gold, fast chomp: a turn running now
chat.help.pacDelegatingDesc: purple with the intercom icon: waiting for a subagent (Task) or another process to return
chat.help.pacQueuedDesc: breathing amber: waiting its turn behind another step
chat.help.pacWaitingDesc: green, slow blink: waiting for your message or your decision
chat.help.pacStaleDesc: dim, still amber: the trail was lost, unknown whether it's still active
chat.help.pacErrorDesc: red and still: stopped due to an error
chat.help.pacDormantDesc: gray and still: nothing active or delegated — the only state without animation
chat.redo.text: 🤔 I think a stronger model would do this better.
